hook.text: That pallet of goods sitting in your warehouse costs $25 per day—rent, insurance, handling, and capital combined.

buildup.text: Holding costs include storage space, insurance, depreciation, obsolescence risk, and the cost of capital.

discovery.text: They typically range from 20–30% of inventory value per year. A $1M stockpile costs $200–300K annually to hold.

twist.text: Most companies underestimate holding costs because they don't account for opportunity cost of tied-up capital.

climax.text: Reducing inventory by just 10% can free up hundreds of thousands in cash for a mid-sized company.

punchline.text: Stored inventory isn't free. Every day on the shelf costs money.

quiz.question: What percentage of inventory value do holding costs typically represent per year?
